issues.item: Compulsive Exercise: I push myself to exercise excessively
issues.explanation: Compulsive exercise is weakly integrated with the rest of the profile. The other selected items cluster around hypervigilance, dissociation, memory disorganisation, and danger-based appraisals after terrorism. Excessive exercise does not clearly serve or connect to those symptoms, making it look like a strategy for a different presentation unless additional context were present.

issues.item: Life Not Worth Living: I am not sure my life is worth living anymore
issues.explanation: 'Life Not Worth Living' is disproportionately severe relative to the rest of the selected profile and is not well supported by the surrounding appraisals. The other appraisals focus on danger and bodily unreliability, while the threat/memory items emphasize hyperarousal and fragmented recall. This suicidal-hopelessness appraisal can occur in PTSD, but here it stands out as insufficiently linked to the rest of the formulation and item set.

vignette: Sofía, a 24-year-old Latina, works at a busy warehouse in Los Angeles. Her life took an unexpected and traumatic turn when she experienced a terrorist attack in her neighborhood last year. The event left indelible marks on her psyche, manifesting through various symptoms that have increasingly impacted her daily functioning. Sofía had come to believe that the world is a dangerous place and that she can no longer trust her own body. This conviction has led her to engage in several maladaptive strategies to cope with her heightened sense of threat. She avoids eye contact with others, feeling that making direct eye contact might expose her to potential danger. Instead, she dissociates deliberately, trying to leave her body or blank out whenever the environment feels too overwhelming. Additionally, Sofía constantly scans her surroundings for signs of any impending threat. The terrorist attack has left her with significant memory gaps; there are parts of the event that she simply cannot remember no matter how hard she tries. When she does recall fragments of it, intense rage surges through her, and she struggles to find words to describe what happened. These memory issues have contributed further to her hypervigilance and maladaptive behaviors. Sofía's belief that the world is dangerous has reinforced her sense of threat. She finds herself feeling immediately on guard when others make sudden movements, and at night, it becomes even harder for her to feel safe. This heightened vigilance often triggers a startle response, making her feel jumpy or easily startled by any unexpected sound or motion. The memory gaps and intense rage that accompany Sofía’s recollections have contributed significantly to her ongoing sense of threat and maladaptive behaviors. She dissociates more frequently as a way to cope with the overwhelming emotions associated with these memories. Her constant scanning for threats is exacerbated by the uncertainty surrounding her recollection of the event, which fuels her hypervigilance. At work, Sofía’s avoidance behaviors are evident in how she navigates the warehouse floor. She avoids eye contact with her coworkers and often finds herself distracted by the need to check her surroundings for any potential danger. This constant vigilance has taken a toll on her job performance; she makes more mistakes than usual due to her divided attention. The cycle of negative appraisals, maladaptive strategies, memory issues, and heightened threat perception has tightened over time. Sofía’s belief that the world is dangerous has led her to avoid social interactions and trust no one fully. This isolation has deepened her sense of mistrust and hypervigilance, making everyday situations feel perilous. Despite these challenges, what frightened Sofía most was the realization that she could not function normally in her daily life without constant fear and avoidance behaviors. Her inability to articulate her experiences clearly had also left her feeling isolated and misunderstood by those around her. It was the mounting strain at work and the increasing sense of isolation that finally brought her to seek help. In therapy, Sofía hopes to regain a sense of safety and control over her life. She is eager to understand why certain triggers still affect her so profoundly and to develop more effective coping strategies. Her primary goal is to find a way to trust her body again and to feel secure in the world around her.
